newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AUSTRALIA RETAIL, BUILDING APPROVALS - Review of forecasts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AUSTRALIA RETAIL, BUILDING APPROVALS - Review of forecasts.

text.p: Australian January retail trade and building approvals data are due at 11.30 a.m. (0030 GMT).

In a week dominated by the release of fourth quarter GDP figures, these partial indicators are seen by many analysts as being just as important because they will give an idea of how the economy is looking in early 1997.

The strength of some of the partial indicators of economic activity, along with the Reserve Bank of Australia's (RBA) outlook on the economy, has seen market expectations turn from another rate cut towards a hike in late 1997 or early 1998.
Recent retail trade and building approvals data follow.
Retail Trade Aug Sep Oct Nov Dec Jan(f)
Building Approvals Aug Sep Oct Nov Dec Jan(f)

After a weak December quarter, and particularly weak pre-Christmas sales, anecdotal evidence suggests that consumers returned to the shops in January and economists expect that to be reflected in a positive retail trade figure.
Forecasts for January centre on a 1.5 percent rise, and range from a rise of 0.2 to 3.0 percent.

The strength is seen coming from a combination of factors, including comments from retailers such as David Jones and Woolworths that trading had picked up since 1997, and that the three rate cuts in 1996 were starting to have some impact.
